text:
Miss X, yes, the little Miss X,

came at last to my hope:

around her eyes,

brief, infinite, knowing nothing.

She is nimble and clean as the gentle

wind at dawn,

cheerful and soft and deep

like grass under water.

She grows sad sometimes

with that mural sadness that on her face

makes quick idols

and draws troubled ghosts.

I think she is like a little girl

asking an old woman questions,

like a scatterbrained little donkey

entering a city, full of straw.

She also has a grown woman

who suddenly frightens her gaze

and stirs inside her and undoes

her insides with bites of weeping.

Miss X, yes, the one who laughs with me

and won't tell me her name,

has now told me, standing on her shadow,

that she loves me but doesn't love me.

I let her shake her head,

saying no and no, since she tires me that way,

and my kiss on her hand sprouts

peacefully beneath the skin, a seed of wings.

Yesterday the light was

wet all day,

and Miss X went out with a cape

over her shoulders, light, in love.

She has never been such a child, never

a lover so loved in all time.

Her hair fell over her forehead,

over her eyes, my soul.


I took her hand, and we walked

all the afternoon of water.


Ah, Miss X, Miss X, hidden

flower of dawn!


You will not love her, sir, you don't know how.

I will see her tomorrow.
